newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen down $1.50, Brent down 10 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen down $1.50, Brent down 10 cts.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures face modest losses at the open on Monday as both markets continued to consolidate after a sharp rally early last week, brokers said.
Oct Brent, which settled Friday at $19.01 a barrel, was seen opening about 10 cents weaker tracking U.S. losses overnight, while Sept gas oil was due about $1.50 below its $171.25 a tonne close.
"We're expecting another gradual move to the downside this morning but whether we make a real break will depend on the volumes," said a broker.
Friday's dealing was subdued by European holidays which kept many players sidelined and volumes thin.
"There was so little interest on Friday that the market wasn't able to achieve its targets," said a broker.
U.S. markets, which set the pace last week as unleaded gasoline rallied nearly eight percent, would continue to provide the lead.

Sept NYMEX crude shed 15 cents to $19.92 in ACCESS dealing and gasoline was also weaker, dropping 0.76 cent to 66.05 cents a gallon despite news late on Friday that Venezuelan exports in September could be affected by refinery problems.

Petroleos de Venezuela's (PdVSA) 45,000 barrels per day (bpd) reforming unit at its Cardon refinery was shut down again on Friday after attempts to restart it resulted in poor quality and capacity performance.
"It will be stopped for another five days and will probably affect next month's loading programme," said a source familiar with the plant's operations.
Dealers were also waiting to see U.S. inventory figures due out late on Tuesday for any evidence of a slowdown in the gasoline season.
